# App Audio Router

> Free, open-source per-app audio routing for Windows 10 / 11 (64-bit): send one program's audio to several playback devices at once, each with its own signed-millisecond delay compensation and its own 0–100 % volume balance. Built as a single native binary on Windows Core Audio — no virtual audio driver, no helper executable, nothing left behind on uninstall. MIT licensed, version 2.1.0, UI in English and Simplified Chinese.

Key facts, all from the project documentation:

- One application → many playback devices simultaneously; the first device is the native Windows endpoint, every further device receives a real-time mirrored copy via WASAPI process-loopback.
- Applies to already-running programs immediately, no restart; stopping returns the program to the system default device.
- Per-device delay compensation (signed milliseconds, configurable range and step) aligns fast devices with slow ones, e.g. wired speakers against a Bluetooth headset.
- Per-device volume balance (0–100 %, relative to the loudest device in the route).
- Routing rules are remembered per executable name and restored automatically; tray-resident with optional close-to-tray and start-with-Windows; device/process lists follow the audio engine's change notifications, never polling.
- Windows-only (Windows 10 / 11, 64-bit); requires only the WebView2 runtime. Not available on macOS or Linux.
